summary: The note surveys recent advances in same-day delivery for local retail and e-commerce, covering hyperlocal logistics, data analytics, drones and autonomous vehicles, personalized services, ship-from-store models and partnerships. It quotes industry figures on how technology and business-model innovation are speeding delivery while improving sustainability and customer experience. It also notes challenges in scaling and balancing speed, cost and quality, and expects immediacy to become a standard expectation.
one_line: Overview of how hyperlocal logistics, analytics, drones, autonomous vehicles, ship-from-store and partnerships are transforming same-day delivery in local retail and e-commerce.
key_facts: QuickStep Logistics was founded by tech entrepreneur Michael Burns in October 2023 and uses AI-powered routing software plus a fleet of eco-friendly electric bikes and scooters.
Michael Burns says fast delivery is becoming sustainable and that the response from local businesses and consumers has been overwhelmingly positive.
As of November 2023, retailers working with DigitalPulse Analytics reported delivery efficiency up by around 25%, with customer satisfaction scores rising due to reduced wait times.
Joanna Harris, CEO of DigitalPulse Analytics, says predictive analytics lets retailers anticipate demand and position products closer to customers.
Drones and autonomous vehicles gained regulatory clearance in late September 2023.

Sarah Kim, Operations Director at TechAir, a Pacific Northwest drone delivery initiative, predicts drones are the future in less dense areas and suburbs because they bypass traffic and reduce manpower.
ShopFast introduced self-driving delivery vans with auto-tech startup DriveAI in December 2023.
NextDoorMart has run a program since January 2024 pairing customers with personal shoppers based on preferences and previous interactions, which has significantly increased customer loyalty.
Simon Grant of OmniRetail Consultants says stores are becoming hybrid spaces, part showroom and part microdistribution centers.
Under the 'ship-from-store' model, online purchases are fulfilled from the store nearest the customer, shaving hours off delivery time and helping lower last-mile carbon footprint.
Nova Logistics CEO Alex Peterson credits a network of partnerships with TrendSet, local pharmacies and electronics outlets for making his company a key player in local same-day delivery.
Retail analyst Jordan Hayes says companies are experimenting with different delivery models to find the sweet spot between speed, cost and service quality.
